newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to reduce deficit to below 3 pct - statement.
newsitem.headline: France to reduce deficit to below 3 pct - statement.

text.p: The French government said on Wednesday it planned to reduce the total public deficit next year to below three percent of gross domestic product.
The central government budget deficit would be 283.7 billion francs, it said in a statement released after a cabinet meeting.
This deficit would have been around 258 billion francs before income tax cuts.
The plans to reduce the total public deficit to below three percent of GDP next year took account of a transfer of funds from France Telecom to cover pension liabilities, it said.

"The government deficit will be brought next year to 283.7 billion francs. Without the reform of income taxes, the government deficit would have been around 258 billion francs after 288 billion in 1996," the statement said.
"The effort to control spending will allow the deficit of all public bodies to remain below three percent of GDP," it said.
"In two and a half years, the deficit will have been reduced from nearly six percent to three percent of GDP," it said.

"This result was obtained by taking account of the exceptional contribution due in 1997 from France Telecom...This contribution will not however be included as a receipt in the central government budget deficit," the statement said.
